Lemma
[Kernel for a compressible torus] Source: chow-et-al-ricci-flow-part-iv:page-0201, chow-et-al-ricci-flow-part-iv:page-0202 1. ch31:31.18\group 3-manifold topology

If $T^2\hookrightarrow M^3$ is compressible and $\pi _1(M)$ is torsion-free, then the kernel of $\pi _1(T)\to \pi _1(M)$ is either all of $\mathbb Z^2$ or an infinite cyclic subgroup generated by a primitive element.
